'''Françoise Balibar''' (born '''Françoise Dumesnil'''; 1941) is a French [[physicist]] and [[History of science|science historian]], a [[Emeritus#In academia|professor emeritus]] at [[Paris Diderot University]].<ref name=culture>{{cite web |url=https://www.franceculture.fr/personne/francoise-balibar |title=Françoise Balibar |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=[[France Culture]] |publisher= |accessdate=2018-02-08 |language=fr}}</ref> She has extensively published works on [[Albert Einstein]], the [[theory of relativity]], and the [[History of physics|history]] and [[epistemology]] of [[physics]].

== Biography ==
Françoise Balibar studied at [[École Normale Supérieure]] from 1960 to 1964.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.babelio.com/auteur/Francoise-Balibar/5309 |title=Françoise Balibar (Babelio) |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=babelio.com |publisher= |accessdate=2018-02-08 |language=fr}}</ref> She has written numerous articles in national and international journals and led the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] team in charge of six volumes of the French edition of Einstein's selected works.<ref name=culture /> She is also the author of several books, including ''The Science of Crystals'' and ''Einstein: Decoding the Universe''.

She is married to philosopher [[Étienne Balibar]] and the mother of the actress [[Jeanne Balibar]]. She has appeared in two films: ''{{ill|Mange ta soupe|fr}}'' in 1997 and ''[[Modern Life (film)|Modern Life]]'' in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0050209/ |title=Françoise Balibar, Actress |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=[[imdb.com]] |publisher= |accessdate=2018-02-08}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* Co-author with [[Jean-Marc Lévy-Leblond]], ''Quantics: Rudiments of Quantum Physics'', North-Holland, 1990
* Co-author with Jean-Pierre Maury, ''How Things Fly'', Barron's Educational Series, 1990
* ''The Science of Crystals'', McGraw-Hill Companies, 1992
* ''Einstein : La joie de la pensée'', collection « [[Découvertes Gallimard]] » (nº 193), série Sciences et techniques. Éditions Gallimard, 1993 (new edition in 2011)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.gallimard.fr/Catalogue/GALLIMARD/Decouvertes-Gallimard/Decouvertes-Gallimard/Sciences-et-techniques/Einstein |title=''Einstein : La joie de la pensée'', collection Découvertes Gallimard (n° 193) |date=4 October 2011 |publisher=[[Éditions Gallimard]] |accessdate=2018-02-08 |language=fr}}</ref>
** US edition – ''Einstein: Decoding the Universe'', “[[Découvertes Gallimard|Abrams Discoveries]]” series. Harry N. Abrams, 2001
** UK edition – ''Einstein: Decoding the Universe'', ‘[[Découvertes Gallimard|New Horizons]]’ series. Thames & Hudson, 2005
* ''Marie Curie : Femme savante ou Sainte Vierge de la science ?'', collection « Découvertes Gallimard » (nº 497), série Sciences et techniques. Éditions Gallimard, 2006
